context: Make the parser format-agnostic (recognize both 'hash filename' and 'MD5 (filename) = hash'), OR standardize all bundled checksums.md5 to GNU format. Either way add a guard test that every bundled TPC-H/TPC-DS checksums.md5 entry matches its on-disk binary, so a stale manifest fails CI instead of silently passing.
description: benchbox/utils/tpc_compilation.py::_verify_checksum parses checksums.md5 by splitting on whitespace (parts[0]=hash, parts[-1]=filename). This matches GNU-format manifests (e.g. darwin-arm64 'hash dbgen') but for BSD-format manifests ('MD5 (dbgen) = hash', used by darwin-x86_64 and others) the filename never matches, so the code silently falls through to 'No checksum entry found' and returns True (assume valid). Effect: the runtime integrity check is a no-op for every BSD-format platform, and a shipped binary that does not match its own manifest (confirmed for darwin-x86_64 packaged dbgen, 2026-07-21) passes unverified. Surfaced during PR #1256 review.

preserves.behavior: A binary whose bytes match its manifest still verifies as valid; only genuine mismatches now fail
